convoLines.text: "Did you sleep? I kept hearing things out past the treeline."
They go still. "So it's not just me. Good. That's... good to know. Bad, but good."
"I sleep in shifts now — two hours, up, listen, two more. My body learned it before my head agreed. Columbus, Ohio never taught me that. The treeline did."
"Still on how you slept. That's the truth of it."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Robin owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Robin said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
"I've got fires to light — metaphorical ones. Mostly."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"So what's your plan here? Just... get through it?"
"Honest. I can work with honest. Not that it matters."
"Flashbulb Moth — It lands. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
"Mine's simple: learn one useful thing a week. This week it's trapping. A plan's just a direction you argue with."
"Still on your plan here."
"I work alone. Nothing personal. ...It's a little personal."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up? Do you understand?"
"I dreamed Robin was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
You show them American Hazelnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Sleep's gone strange. I sleep with one ear uncovered, always at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"We're done for now. Not done-done. For now."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
"Got a read on anyone here yet? Who should I be watching?"
"Same. But keep your eyes open — some people here are performing, not surviving."
"Watch the quiet ones. Not the loud — the loud tell you everything. The quiet are either thinking or planning, and you can't tell which until it matters."
"Still on your read on people here."
"I don't know you well enough for that. Ask me again when we've survived something together."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Since Robin died... I keep expecting to see Robin at the fire. Stupid."
You show them American Hazelnut — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"I write everything down. It doesn't bring anyone back. It just keeps my hands from shaking."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Anyway — I should get going."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"About that question — Do you still count the days? I lost track days ago."
"Good. Keep counting. The days need witnesses."
"Sunbasker — Its scales go from dull brown to molten gold. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
Whatever warmth was building cools to politeness.
"Still on what day it is."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? It'll pass."
"Good question." It's not that I don't like people. It's that I like breathing more.
"I like people fine. In doses. Small doses. With exits."
"I need the quiet the way other people need food. Don't worry about me."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"We never finished talking about what's been happening — we left it mid-thought, 4 days back. 'You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.'"
"Nobody says Robin's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
"I'm picking up Robin's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
You show them Dandelion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good — what's been happening, settled. Feels better said out loud."
"This was good." They mean it.
"We never did finish talking about what's been happening — that was 12 days back. Still on your mind? 'We're done for now. Not done-done. For now.'"
"This one — Pedunculate Oak Acorn. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
You show them Lamb's Quarters — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Same as always: we endure."
"I do the small things right. The big things notice."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." I'm fine on my own. I was fine before all this. Don't take it personally.
"We started on what's been happening, then got onto what they want."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Right. Go on, then."
"This was good." They mean it.
"What did you do for fun? Before. The thing you'd do on a perfect Saturday."
"The free things. Turns out they were the expensive ones."
"There's more, but that's for another fire."
"Real talk — I was a bike messenger — fun was whatever I could steal between shifts. Now fun is watching the fire and not being afraid. It's a downgrade and an upgrade."
"Still on what you did for fun. Good talking."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Good question." "They took me. The Pit — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
«Гей... ти розмовляєш українською? Ні? ...бляха.» (you catch 'Ні' — no) "Thank you?" — they grin, proud of the one English they know.
«Саме так. В точку.» (you catch 'точку' — point) They nod back, slowly.
«Все буде добре.» (you catch 'добре' — good) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«Дякую, що ти тут.» (Thanks that you're here. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Ти розумієш?» (Do you understand? — you're fairly sure)
Their gestures slow — the conversation thinning like light at dusk.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said fun was just being around your people. Do we count? Are we trying?"
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Sassafras — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Enzo always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"This was good." They mean it.
"You heard the sounds past the treeline too, that night. They haven't stopped, have they?"
Maya has an edge today — something curdled.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind? Not that it matters."
"You want to know about that? Okay." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "Enzo is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Cattail — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
«Добре, що ти тут. Справді.» (Good that you're here. Really. — you're fairly sure)
«Правильно.» (Correct. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.
«Я цього тобі ніколи не забуду.» (I'll never forget you for this. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm. "Food?"
«Ти справді добра людина.» (You're truly a good person. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic.
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «Де тут сплять? Безпечно?» (Where do they sleep here? Safe? — you're fairly sure)
A final shared look — you both feel the talk running its course.
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
«会えてよかった。本当に。» (Glad we met. Really. — you're fairly sure)
«まさにそう。» (Precisely so. — you're fairly sure) They nod back, slowly.
«この恩は忘れない。» (I won't forget this debt. — you're fairly sure) A grin breaks through, quick and warm.
«いてくれてありがとう。» (Thanks for being here. — you're fairly sure) You tap your chest, then theirs. Us. They nod, emphatic. "Thank you?"
You listen hard, watching their mouth shape the words. «食べ物ある？何か？» (Have food? Anything? — you're fairly sure)
Yuki blinks. Then cracks up. "You said that BEAUTIFULLY. It means nothing like what you think it means." They teach you the right word, still laughing.
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Sure. I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."

deathBeat: d16: 📖 The Codex turns a page on its own. Robin Schulz is dead. You didn't ask. It knew.
d16: 🕯️ Robin Schulz is dead — contest. The village stops. Somebody screams. Somebody else starts digging.
d16: The village's quarrel was with Robin — and Robin is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
recoverHome: d17: That night, they bring Robin home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
systemVoice: d16: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 52. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 4."
d17: SYSTEM: Codex and inventory overlay online.
d17: ◈ AUDIENCE TRIAL — SYSTEM: "A trial, broadcast live. The audience loves a trial." Haul 1,000 kcal to the pantry within 3 days. Reward: integration, and a lesson.

d17: ◈ RESONANCE HARMONICS — SYSTEM: "HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. Objects with high observer-attention waveforms function as auxiliary capacitors. We call this RESONANCE HARMONICS. We do not know why the waveforms taste like grief. We have stopped asking." — Hold a keepsake. Think about them. The System will d
d17: SYSTEM: "DEMONSTRATION. Give me that — Trail compass. WATCH."
d17: SYSTEM: Oh! It has a NAME. You all love names.
d18: 📺 SYSTEM: "We have already cleared your morning. You are welcome. We require 300 kcal of tubers and your full attention. The fans love a cooking segment."
d18: ⬢ SYSTEM: "Neural depth 68. I can hold more of you now — ability slots: 5."
burialWindowSay: d16: The village's quarrel was with Robin — and Robin is dead. The sentence doesn't cross the grave. You're someone else now; the docket is empty, but the village remembers.
d16: ◈ The System files the name away with visible satisfaction. It has so few words for things that bleed. (+5 integration)
d17: That night, they bring Robin home. Nobody asks you to help carry; nobody has to. By morning the grave is dug by the fire, and the body is laid out beside it. The filling of it is yours.
d19: You say a few words for Robin. Not a ceremony — just: you were here, and someone noticed you leaving. (-3 trauma)
d19: You bury Robin. A marker, of sorts. The village will know where. (+4 trauma)
echoSample: d19: "You want to know about that? Okay." "Robin owed me a favor. I keep thinking about collecting. Stupid."
d19: "I keep turning over the last thing Robin said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
d19: "I dreamed Robin was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
d19: "Since Robin died... I keep expecting to see Robin at the fire. Stupid."
d23: "Nobody says Robin's name right yet. We will. Give it a few days."
d23: "I'm picking up Robin's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
echoV2Sample: d19: The village raises a marker by the fire — Robin, day 19. contest. A place to stand.
